youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Alia Bland’s open letter about Jacinda Ardern’s new academic role (which passed 1.2 million views) sets a positive tone as host Maree Buscke also welcomes Rodney Hide and Kathryn Ennis-Carter. The panel unpacks overhang seats, so-called wasted votes and strategic voting through lolly-themed videos, before Alia demonstrates the new Vote Check electorate tool and Kathryn weighs in on local government. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart . You can also see if your electorate is a close contest at Votecheck For more information: Check out Alia’s open letter on X and Facebook More RCR Election 2026 interviews For previous RCR webinars Jaspreet Boparai's opinion on TOP

youtube.title: SUZANNE LEVY
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by with Speak Up for Women spokeswoman Suzanne Levy to discuss their High Court challenge to police and customs strip-search policies, which use gender identity rather than sex. Suzanne explains why attempts to resolve the issue with authorities failed, discusses the legal implications for women’s privacy and protections and examines how the election and proposed definitions legislation could shape the future of sex-based rights in New Zealand. Discover more from Suzanne at Speak up for Women or find them on Facebook and X

youtube.title: MAURICE WILLIAMSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with former National MP and cabinet minister Maurice Williamson about the latest election polls and how MMP’s overhang rules could affect the result. Williamson argues that National could win more electorates than its party vote entitles it to, leaving it without list MPs. He defends strategic vote-splitting as legitimate under the current system and proposes changing MMP from a “minus” to a “plus” model so both votes count. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson discuss Jacinda Ardern’s University of Sydney appointment, the erosion of working-class politics, rising fuel costs and the need for greater energy security. They examine the election’s two-bloc contest, the potential impact of the MMP overhang strategy and the importance of strengthening NZ First and ACT within the coalition. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart Alia's Open Letter to the University of Sydney on X RNZ | Literally illiterate – Luxon lashes Labour's economic record

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart takes aim at Jacinda Ardern’s appointment as a professor of practice at the University of Sydney and controversial changes to Australian sex discrimination law. She criticises gender identity policies and male lactation, questioning the implications for women’s rights, infant safety and the legal recognition of biological sex. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: DAVID FARRAR
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Curia Market Research founder David Farrar about New Zealand’s knife-edge election and the risks of tactical voting. David warns that deliberately engineered overhangs could undermine proportional representation, weaken National by costing it experienced MPs and fuel political polarisation. He discusses possible electoral reforms, Germany’s approach and four scenarios for government formation, including the potential influence of The Opportunity Party. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart For more from David Farr visit KiwiBlog and Curia

youtube.summary: "I feel like I'm at an AA meeting for National Party members. G'day, my name is Alf." - Alfred Ngaro, NZ First Candidate and Former Cabinet Minister Step one: admit you used to vote National. Step two: explain where the values went. youtube.title: "Do you want the big giant douche or do you want the turd sandwich?" - Marty Gibson
youtube.summary: "Do you want the big giant douche or do you want the turd sandwich?" - Marty Gibson Not exactly the line either campaign will be putting on a billboard. Gibson and Buscke argue that when the two major parties increasingly occupy the same ground, MMP's smaller parties become the handbrake, steering wheel and occasionally the emergency exit. Are voters finally realising their second vote can matter more than ever? Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson are back with Media Matters. 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/media-matters-are-the-major-parties-really-offering-a-choice #RCRMedia #MediaMatters

youtube.summary: "I think the National Party's two-tick strategy is just brain dead and could possibly lose the election for the centre-right." - Michael Laws, NZ First Candidate, Otago Councillor & Broadcaster Laws says the maths of MMP and a possible Te Pāti Māori overhang make National's insistence on two ticks blue a potentially costly gamble. Could National's own strategy end up handing power to the centre-left? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/michael-laws-nz-first-candidate-otago-councillor-broadcaster-rogernomics-the-beginning-of-the-end #RCRMedia

youtube.title: RCR Wednesday Webinars - Politics: Vote Smart 2026
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by Rodney Hide, Alia Bland and Katherine Ennis-Carter for a wide-ranging political discussion that begins with Alia's viral open letter following Ardern's appointment to an academic role focused on empathy and social cohesion. From there, the panel turns to the election itself, discussing the prospect of a Labour-led government, the latest polling, MMP, overhang seats, strategic voting and the electorate contests that could influence the makeup of the next Parliament. A lively discussion about the political past, the choices facing voters today, and what's at stake on 7 November.

youtube.title: "Is it a key or is it a deed?" - Patrick Wood, Researcher, Author & Founder of Technocracy News
youtube.summary: "Is it a key or is it a deed?" - Patrick Wood, Researcher, Author & Founder of Technocracy News Wood says people need to take stock of what they truly own versus what they merely have access to. If your access can be revoked, is it really ownership at all? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/patrick-wood-researcher-author-founder-of-technocracy-news-will-you-still-own-your-home-in-a-tokenised-economy #RCRMedia

youtube.title: "They only get to the start line in about 100,000 from now." - Maurice Williamson, Former National M
youtube.summary: "They only get to the start line in about 100,000 from now." - Maurice Williamson, Former National MP Williamson says National's electorate strength means it may need around another 100,000 party votes before gaining even one additional MP from them. If that's correct, does "two ticks blue" still make mathematical sense? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/a-political-agenda-with-bob-mccoskrie-maurice-williamson-strategic-voting-why-this-election-is-different #RCRMedia

youtube.title: KARLEEN GRIBBLE
youtube.summary: Professor Karleen Gribble, an academic and researcher at Western Sydney University, speaks with Michael Arbon about the recording of sex in Australian health data and the risks of inaccurate records. They discuss the shift towards gender-neutral language in healthcare, its implications for medical safety and research and how replacing terms such as “women” and “mothers” may affect public health communication and support for mothers. Discover more from Karleen Gribble Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with NZ First leader Winston Peters on the party’s election campaign, covering the Covid-19 vaccine rollout, puberty blockers, fuel security and domestic oil exploration. Winston defends merit-based recruitment over diversity, equity and inclusion policies, highlights his party’s economic expertise and calls for growth above 3%. He dismisses current polling as unreliable, predicting NZ First will surprise its critics on election night. Discover more from Winston Peters on X , Facebook and Instagram For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart discuss election turnout, voter enrolment and misunderstandings about MMP, arguing for strategic voting to strengthen the current coalition. They examine the potential gains for ACT and New Zealand First, Labour’s handling of gang controversies and concerns about The Opportunities Party’s policies and censorship. They also share campaign observations, including a debt-monster costume shadowing Chris Hipkins.​ For further information: Check out Trevor Mallard's comments on X around advance voting For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X
